Hi,

I don't know but I would guess that is possible. INLA does not use any
shapefile, only for some models you need to input the graph of the
model. it might be it would be as easy to extract the graph from the
SXLE file directly, but I am just guessing.

messages.subject: Re: Winbugs map to R-INLA
parts:
I have figured it out. For anyone who may encounter the same challenge, say you wanted to use the Scotland map (provided in WinBUGS) in R-INLA. Open WinBUGS, go to map and slick on adjacency tool, select Scotland
map, click adj map. The Scotland map should appear. Go to map again and click on export Splus. Save the result as Scotland.txt etc document. Read the txt file in R as ken<- readSplus("C:/Users/Gem/Desktop/shpfiler/angola.txt")


Alternatively these codes may be of use too.

Dear Okango,

If your map is from WinBUGS you can export it into Splus format (please see how to do it in http://www.mrc-bsu.cam.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/geobugs12manual.pdf)

Them you can read it as SpatialPolygons in R using the readSplus() funciton from the 'maptools' package.

Elias
